why: All infected cells spread at the same time, one ring per minute, so put every initial infected cell in the queue at distance 0 and BFS: the minutes needed is the largest BFS level that reaches a fresh cell.
hints: Infection spreads one step per minute from every infected cell at once. Which traversal naturally moves outward one layer at a time?
Start a single BFS with all initially infected cells in the queue (multi-source). The minute a fresh cell is infected equals its BFS distance from the nearest infected cell.
Count fresh cells, seed the deque with all 2s, process level by level, decrement the fresh count on each infection; return the last level if fresh hits 0, else -1. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: No fresh cells at all returns 0, even when there are no infected cells either.
Running a separate BFS from each infected cell and taking a max is both slow and wrong; the sources must expand simultaneously.
Do not count a final empty level as an extra minute; the answer is the level of the last infection, not the number of loop iterations.
constraints:
• 1 <= rows, cols <= 1000 (numeric bounds not stated in the source)
  • Each cell is 0, 1 or 2
